title: Fishing rod
prompt: A labelled bench teaching model of the page 23 fishing rod has two visible hand grips and a line suspending a fish-shaped test mass above a small tank. Load attaches the mass. Lift keeps the rear hand fixed as fulcrum while the forward hand supplies effort to turn the rod and raise the tip. Compare travel repeats slowly with effort-hand and tip travel arrows and moment arms. Show the force disadvantage and greater load travel of a third-class lever. The mass and tank are teaching props. Keep casting and reel mechanisms outside this figure.
blurb: A bench teaching adaptation of a fishing rod shows how a third-class lever trades force for greater tip travel.

identity.note: Levers / Third-class levers, page 21, and Fishing rod, page 23. One hand is the fulcrum, the other applies effort, and the fish load travels farther than the effort hand.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct from hammer and tweezers despite the shared third-class principle. Two hand positions and a suspended fish load identify the source application.

prompt.note: Lift is supported. Casting, hooking and bending could dominate the original scene without teaching the supported lever lesson. Use a pre-attached visible load and travel comparison. A reel drive is not the explanation.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

teachingAdaptation.geometry: A representative solid tapered pole with line lashed at its tip. No reel or casting mechanism. Dimensions are teaching choices, not book measurements.
teachingAdaptation.idealization: Rigid weightless rod, massless taut line, slow lift, negligible friction and inertia. Both applied forces are vertical.

actions.Load: Attach the loose line to the eye of the mass resting above the tank.
actions.Lift: Rotate about the fixed rear hand through 26 degrees in 1.8 seconds.
actions.Compare travel: Lower then repeat the lift over four seconds with hand and tip arcs and horizontal moment arms.
actions.Reset: Lower the attached mass to its cradle, then detach the line.

quantities.momentArms: Perpendicular horizontal distances to the vertical force lines. Arc travel is measured along the circular hand and tip paths.

representativeConstructionSources.supports: For a cane pole or stick, the fishing line can be tied directly to its end. This supports the simplified fixed-line construction, not the book apparatus dimensions.
A reel-free fishing pole can use line tied directly to its tip. The representative product has a butt cap; the model does not reproduce its telescoping construction.
